why: EQUIVALENT, not a coverage gap, and measured rather than assumed: it was declared `killed` first and SURVIVED. `relaunchTarget === 'versus-setup'` already means a pane-originated versus session (`relaunchTargetFor`: versus identity plus a `sessionOrigin` other than `'versus-flags'`), and the start boundary never creates one without a config -- so `deps.initialVersusConfig` cannot be null when this branch is reached. The field is optional only because `GameDeps` makes it optional for the campaign path, which is why the guard exists at all: TypeScript needs it to call through. A `?dev=1&mode=ffa` world takes the campaign branch because its relaunch target differs, not because of this guard. Kept so that a future change making a config-less `'versus-setup'` session reachable is what flips this to killed, rather than a silent fabrication of a configuration the player never chose.
